verdicts.factCheck: USDG. eth_call on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc at block 526,831,684: 0x004b506865409877c9fa29bfb1eba929984b9bbc reports name Global Dollar, 6 decimals, total supply 65,785,893.96, isFrozen(PoolManager) false, paused false in globalTransferSettings(), owner 0x6c9e821ade9efc1bcda763f9942dd7822d6e86b4 and payoutGroupIdOf(PoolManager) 0. balanceOf(PoolManager) is 1,685,060.10, which is 27,000 less than the finding quotes and moves with trading. The Paxos documentation lists this address as USDG on Arbitrum. The implementation 0x031610e2d186d78d3defbf907f56d1eac843d9de is an exact match on Sourcify. Its transfer carries whenNotPaused and _transfer reverts with AddressFrozen when the sender or the recipient is frozen (PaxosTokenClaimableRewards.sol line 142, ClaimableRewardsBase.sol line 476). From an ordinary account freeze, unfreeze, freezeBatch and wipeFrozenAddress revert for a missing role 0xe3e4f9d7..., which is the hash of ASSET_PROTECTION_ROLE, and pause reverts for a missing PAUSE_ROLE. A transfer of 1 unit sent from the PoolManager address succeeds today. USD+. 0xfc90518d5136585ba45e34ed5e1d108bd3950cfa has implementation slot 0xff5bff8081eaee966bd74e9c0c059949df2345e1, publicVersion 6.0.0, total supply 3,113,037.91, balancePerShare 1.0706777538e18, sharesOf(PoolManager) 999,999.892917 and balanceOf(PoolManager) 1,070,677.639195, which is 34.4 percent of supply. I overrode the storage slot 0x5317...bb02 that holds the index in an eth_call: with the index at 1.0, 0.5 and 2.0 the PoolManager balance reads 999,999.89, 499,999.95 and 1,999,999.79. The deployed code therefore computes the balance as shares times that slot. rebaseAdd(uint128,bytes32) and rebaseSub(uint128,bytes32) exist and revert with AC: unauthorized for an ordinary account, the one argument forms revert with empty data, mint reverts, and burn(address,uint256) reverts for want of an allowance. transferRestrictor() is 0x2ed5c85d5105abe5d13586c5c3a8f99a837942b4, its owner and default admin is 0x269e944ad9140fc6e21794e8ea71ce1afbfe38c8, and restrict(address) reverts for an ordinary account for a missing RESTRICTOR_ROLE. The public Dinari source is version 2 and differs from the deployed version 6, as the finding says. The downward move of the index is no longer hypothetical. An archive node (https://arb-pokt.nodies.app, eth_getStorageAt) shows the index slot at 1.0706777538e18 up to block 425,966,863, at exactly 1.0707e18 from block 425,966,864, and back at 1.0706777538e18 from block 426,017,089 (2026-01-28, 02:42 and 06:11 UTC). The PoolManager received its USD+ in one transfer of 1,070,700.000000 at block 425,967,321, 457 blocks after the rise, which gave it exactly 1,000,000 shares. The fall 3.5 hours later cut its balance by 22.25 USD+. Neither move emitted BalancePerShareSet, and neither used rebaseAdd or rebaseSub. Both were made by transactions 0x16f245ef068749c80ba697e5b14962b48e2173410b59c0d80736a4c388a76903 and 0xef84fb3eb1d357044c6f0dabccca656f41641c218bda362a82eaf006ee039837, sent by the account 0x4d0d668410c765cdee19c0ef2f0523fc231e879f to Multicall3, which called 0xb7541f225385104347539397a4e01abc1d4ea8bd with selector 0x4348352c, the token address, an ECDSA signature and an inner call 0x8078438b that names one storage slot of the token, its expected old value and its new value. USD+ accepts selector 0x8078438b when the caller is 0xb7541f... (eth_call with that sender returns without revert today) and rejects it from any other sender I tried.
verdicts.codeCheck: One address holds every pool's balance of a currency, and each payout is a plain transfer from it. take debits the caller and calls currency.transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). For an ERC-20 the call must succeed and return nothing or a 32 byte true, otherwise the function reverts with the wrapped error (src/types/Currency.sol:60-74 and 82-86). collectProtocolFees uses the same transfer (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56). A frozen or paused USDG and a restricted USD+ revert inside transfer, so every take and fee collection in that token reverts. No guard in src/ offers another exit: mint moves a claim and leaves the token where it is (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329). For the index: sync stores balanceOf(PoolManager) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/types/Currency.sol:90-96) and _settle credits reservesNow minus reservesBefore (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364). The subtraction at line 360 is checked, so a fall of the balance between sync and settle reverts the settle and credits nothing. A rise between the two is credited to the settler. Pool accounting never reads the token balance again, so after a downward move the pools record more USD+ than the PoolManager holds and the last take for the difference fails in the token. I read these lines in this checkout and found no guard that the finding missed. The live PoolManager is other bytecode than a build of this checkout, so the on-chain reads describe the tokens and the deployed manager.
verdicts.corrections: The actor is right: every lever needs a Paxos role, the Dinari restrictor role, or a signature that 0xb7541f225385104347539397a4e01abc1d4ea8bd accepts. Four statements need correcting. First, the mechanism says about 70,678 USD+ of the pooled balance is index growth that belongs to no pool. That is wrong. The whole balance arrived in one transfer at block 425,967,321, after the last BalancePerShareSet event (block 425,539,068). Transfer logs give a net inflow of 1,070,699.885347 and the balance is 1,070,677.639195, so the PoolManager is 22.25 USD+ short of what the pools were credited, and there is no surplus. Second, the lever that moved the index is a raw storage write to the token, authorised by an off-chain signature and submitted through a public contract. It can write the index slot and, by its shape, any other slot named in the call. The finding describes only the role gated rebase functions, and the statement that the index did not move rests on an event that this route does not emit. The call is open to any sender: an eth_call of the first transaction's calldata from an unrelated address at block 425,966,863 succeeds, both through Multicall3 and directly. A tampered signature or payload reverts, a zero signature reverts with ECDSAInvalidSignature, and both used calls revert from every sender after their first execution, so they cannot be replayed. I could not read the contract (no verified source for 0xb7541f..., its implementation 0x1b5a16e81ab8154559ec2f457fa61062a6b8876f or the token implementation), so the signer, the digest format and its other functions are unconfirmed. Third, USDG on Arbitrum One is the Paxos claimable rewards build, and the asset protection role also holds wipeFrozenAddress, so the issuer can burn a frozen balance as well as block it. On the restrictor, restrict(address) needs RESTRICTOR_ROLE, which the admin 0x269e... grants. Fourth, the value of the USD+ position is face value. All of it sits in one hookless USDC/USD+ pool (id 0x12d6df73..., fee 0.3 percent), in one position of the account 0xcd04ccbf1cd5d18c9735b59f5e41f03a2941ebad between ticks 1080 and 3540, and the pool price is at tick 3539, which is 0.70 USDC per USD+. The title's 2.78M is 1.69M USDG plus 1.07M USD+ at par today.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-139, unprivileged part: can an ordinary account change balanceOf(PoolManager) of Dinari USD+ or of xUSD without a transfer, so that a settle is credited for it, or burn the PoolManager balance.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The answer for USD+ rests on the reverts of rebaseAdd and rebaseSub and on the absence of index events. The index moved twice on 2026-01-28 (blocks 425,966,864 and 426,017,089) through another route that emits no event: a signed storage write submitted to 0xb7541f225385104347539397a4e01abc1d4ea8bd, which the token accepts as caller of selector 0x8078438b. The submission is open to any sender. An eth_call of the first transaction's calldata from an unrelated address succeeds at block 425,966,863 on the archive node https://arb-pokt.nodies.app. An ordinary account that holds an unused signed write that raises the index can place it between its own sync and settle and is credited the rise on the whole pooled balance (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 358-364). I found no way for an ordinary account to obtain one: forged and altered signatures revert, the two used ones revert on replay from block 426,017,089 to today, and Arbitrum One has no public mempool. The gain would be the index step times the pooled balance, 22.25 USD+ for the step seen, and the only step since the deposit went down, which makes a settle revert. So the item's conclusion holds for what I could test and its stated basis does not. The second fact in it is also off: the pooled balance did not grow with the index, it fell by 22.25 USD+. The xUSD part was not rechecked.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Transaction types, walked for msg.sender, msg.value and transient storage in unlock, sync, settle and take at Nitro v3.12.4 and fork commit 0e44603: legacy, access list, dynamic fee and set code transactions, blob transactions, deposits (0x64), unsigned (0x65) and contract (0x66) transactions, retries (0x68), retryable submissions (0x69), internal transactions (0x6a), transactions on the on-chain filter list, and the message kinds batch, heartbeat, nonmutating call and compressed transaction.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/state_transition.go and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/v3.12.4/arbos/tx_processor.go. execute() calls StartTxHook first (line 837) and returns at once for deposits, retryable submissions and internal transactions (lines 840-862). In StartTxHook the deposit case mints and transfers a balance with no EVM call (tx_processor.go lines 237-268), the internal case allows only the sender 0xa4b05 (lines 269-275), and the retry case moves the escrow and continues (lines 538-570). Every other path reaches st.state.Prepare at line 950, which replaces the transient map (core/state/statedb.go line 1650), before the single top call at line 1004. The one contract call inside an internal transaction, ProcessParentBlockHash, runs its own Prepare first (core/state_processor.go line 358). tx_processor.go makes no evm.Call of its own. This matches Lock, CurrencyDelta, CurrencyReserves and NonzeroDeltaCount starting at zero in each transaction. I could not confirm that v3.12.4 pins commit 0e44603, because the repository page was not reachable and .gitmodules names no commit, and the live build v3.13.0-rc.9 is unpublished.

clearedSpotChecks.check: EIP-7702 on Nitro: an account whose delegation points at a precompile, including an ArbOS precompile, used as the currency of a take, as the target of sync, or as the recipient of a native take.
clearedSpotChecks.note: resolveCode returns nil for a delegation that points at a precompile from ArbOS 50 on (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/vm/evm.go lines 789-806). I repeated the probe with eth_call and a state override on the three RPC endpoints: an account with code 0xef0100 followed by 0x64, 0x6e or 0x02 answers transfer, balanceOf and empty calldata from the PoolManager address with success and empty return data, and sync of that account on the deployed PoolManager reverts, as does sync of an address without code. A direct call to ArbSys with the transfer selector or with empty calldata reverts. In src/ a take of such a currency passes the empty return test (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74) and leaves a negative delta under that currency id (src/PoolManager.sol:294). The debt can be closed only by a settle after sync, which reverts at src/types/Currency.sol:94, or by burning claims of that id, which nobody can hold without a prior credit. unlock then reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:112. My probe used the PoolManager as the outer sender and no forwarding stub.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Critic gap of cycle 5: can any transaction type, system call or precompile call a contract with msg.sender equal to the zero address, which is the stored protocol fee controller on Elysium (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48).
clearedSpotChecks.note: parse_l2.go takes the sender of unsigned and contract transactions from the poster argument (lines 245-264), of deposits from header.Poster (line 292) and of retryable submissions from header.Poster (line 364), and tx_processor.go rejects an internal transaction whose sender is not the ArbOS address (lines 269-275). The checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48 compare msg.sender with the stored controller and nothing else, so on Elysium they pass only for a call from the zero address. I did not repeat the balance and nonce reads of 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeef on HyperEVM.

leads.question: Who signs the storage writes that 0xb7541f225385104347539397a4e01abc1d4ea8bd (implementation 0x1b5a16e81ab8154559ec2f457fa61062a6b8876f) executes on Dinari USD+ at 0xfc90518d5136585ba45e34ed5e1d108bd3950cfa, how do the signed messages reach the submitting account 0x4d0d668410c765cdee19c0ef2f0523fc231e879f, and does any other function of that contract make it call the token with caller chosen data?
leads.why: The token accepts selector 0x8078438b from that contract and the call names raw storage slots, so the holder of the signer account can set the index, a share balance or the restrictor address. Submission is open to any sender. An account that obtains an unused signed write raising the index can run it between its own sync and settle and be credited the rise on 1.07M pooled USD+ (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 358-364). The cleared item on USD+ did not know this route. Decompile the two implementations, find the digest and the replay guard, recover the signer from the two used signatures, and check whether signed messages are published anywhere before they land.

leads.question: The PoolManager holds 1,070,677.64 USD+ against a net inflow of 1,070,699.89 by Transfer logs. Is the 22.25 USD+ shortfall booked to the one position in pool 0x12d6df7390ed2fd24b259c0737dcaaf58116ca29cd96c758c5bf5a948fb28b8c (USDC/USD+, fee 0.3 percent, no hook, PositionManager token 127727 of 0xcd04ccbf1cd5d18c9735b59f5e41f03a2941ebad), and is that account tied to the party that moved the index?
leads.why: The index was raised to exactly 1.0707 two minutes before the deposit of exactly 1,000,000 shares and lowered 3.5 hours later, and the pool has offered USD+ at about 0.70 USDC since with almost no trades. If the liquidity provider and the signer are one party, the exposure of others is limited to swappers in that pool. If they are not, this is a recorded case of an issuer side balance cut inside the PoolManager and belongs with F-086 and F-087. A full removal of the position must take 22.25 USD+ more than the PoolManager holds, which meets the limit described in F-083.

leads.question: USDG on Arbitrum One is the Paxos claimable rewards build with payout groups. Which accounts hold PAYOUT_GROUP_REGISTRAR_ROLE and CLAIM_OPERATOR_ROLE, can the PoolManager address be put into a payout group without a call from it, and who then receives the rewards that accrue on the pooled 1.69M USDG?
leads.why: balanceOf excludes unclaimed rewards and a claim moves USDG from the claim source to a destination the claimer names (ClaimableRewardsBase.sol lines 314-378 and 429-457 in the Sourcify source of 0x031610e2d186d78d3defbf907f56d1eac843d9de). Today payoutGroupIdOf(PoolManager) is 0 and partner signed registrations are off, so nothing accrues. A registration would direct yield on pooled funds to a third party, and a claim with the PoolManager as destination between a sync and a settle would be credited to the settler. The facets that hold registration and claims were not read.
